messages.author: b2e3af1a025642ca
messages.subject: Accelerometer H10 Polar analysis
parts:
Hi, thank you for accepting my group membership request. 


I introduce myself, my name is Giorgio Sanseverino and I am writing from Italy. I am a graduate in Exercise Sciences.


Before putting forward my question, I would like to thank Dr Vincent van Hees and the collaborators of the project for having accomplished this invaluable work.


So, I have a polar H10 chest strap that contains a triaxial accelerometer inside.


In general, its use is encouraged as a low-cost valid tool for HRV analysis, given that this sensor has been validated against the ECG gold standard.

However, it may also be interesting to evaluate its accelerometer. So far no research has been conducted in this regard.


It is capable of measuring acceleration with sample rates of 25Hz, 50Hz, 100Hz and 200Hz, and range of 2G, 4G and 8G. Axis specific acceleration data are in mG.


The application, which I use to record the signal sent by the sensor, exports the raw data to .txt


This data appears in the notebook separated by a single space in the following way:


timestamp x y z

643045806839701885 -961 5 186

643045806849669402 -956 8 195

643045806859636919 -957 14 214

643045806869604436 -969 15 211

643045806879571953 -982 20 187

643045806889539470 -984 25 181

643045806899506987 -983 32 202

643045806909474504 -984 32 218


Timestamp format is nanoseconds and the epoch is 1.1.2000.


Do you think It’s possible to make this files .txt compatible for analysis in GGIR?


Thanks

Giorgio Sanseverino

messages.author: 13568954e9b4ef4b
messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] Accelerometer H10 Polar analysis
parts:
Hi Giorgio,
This should be possible. See documentation for GGIR function read.myacc.csv, which facilitates reading custom csv data formats. All you will have to do is export the txt file to a csv file and make sure the arguments for the read.myacc.csv function allign with the csv format.
Best wishes, Vincent
